meaning: From Hexanchus: Greek héx “six” + anchus, of unclear origin, perhaps ánchō “to choke”, for the six gill openings that reach down onto the throat; -formes “shaped like”
description: Sharks with six or seven pairs of gill slits instead of the usual five, and a single dorsal fin without a spine, set well back on the body. Frilled sharks and the cow sharks (sixgill and sevengill sharks) belong here.
